justification: Onboards Wingecarribee to the numeric DCP-controls dataset (the 29th LGA) so the Bowral demo lot gets real setback/landscaping/parking/height numbers. 32 hand-curated rows extracted VERBATIM from the in-force town plans (Bowral/Mittagong/Moss Vale, amended 2015), each with source quote + section ref + PDF page, loaded via the established per-council insert-script pattern. Preceded by a full Phase-0 smoke test with live data (ce-wingecarribee-numeric-onboarding-2026-07.md): the three town plans were fetched from the Portal /dcp planURLs, proven 100% machine-readable, and their residential values proven IDENTICAL across the three towns (single-slug design validated). One genuine source defect found (C3.9.2(c)(ii) omits its height threshold in all three published documents) — loaded with needs_review=TRUE and verified WITHHELD by the fetcher (#707 fail-closed). End-to-end verified in production: address -> slug wingecarribee -> fetch_dcp_setbacks returns 31 controls (flagged row excluded).

pre_impl.existing_data: Everything reused: the dcp_setback_controls schema (constrained enums for applicability/extraction_method discovered live and complied with), the lga_registry FK pattern, the insert-script pattern (insert_ashfield_sd_setbacks.py), the DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS completeness gate at generate_conveyancing_report.py:270, and the needs_review fail-closed handling shipped in #707. The Phase-0 probe also reused the Portal /dcp endpoint discovered in May and the pypdf tooling already in the environment.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Three assumptions corrected by live data: (1) the Portal /dcp endpoint does NOT resolve which town plan governs a property — it returns the council's whole 18-document catalogue, so per-town scoping had to come from the documents themselves; (2) neutralized by the decisive finding that the three town plans share one Part C template with identical residential values (verified verbatim in all three), making a single wingecarribee slug safe; (3) applicability and extraction_method turned out to be constrained enums and lga has an FK to lga_registry — all discovered by the first insert attempts and complied with rather than worked around.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: one insert script (32 data rows, self-contained with an idempotent lga_registry registration) and one slug added to the existing DCP_ONBOARDED_SLUGS gate. Explicitly NOT built: any full-text DCP extraction (deferred until the consolidated Wingecarribee DCP 2026 is adopted — onboarding 17 soon-to-be-replaced documents is throwaway), any secondary-dwelling rows (the town plans' Part C sections extracted do not carry SD-specific numerics — absence fails closed), and any village/rural DCP rows (unverified against the template; town-plan scope only).

functions.name: main
functions.input: Optional --dry-run flag; DATABASE_URL or SUPABASE_DB_URL from the environment
functions.output: Idempotent load: lga_registry upsert plus 32 dcp_setback_controls rows with verbatim source_text, section_ref, pdf_page, dcp_version and needs_review flags; prints per-row outcome and totals
functions.if_none: Missing DB URL exits 1 before touching anything; the dup-check skips rows that already exist (keyed on lga+dev_type+control_type+condition) so re-running cannot double-insert; dry-run prints the full row table with zero writes

values.value: needs_review=TRUE on the C3.9.2(c)(ii) side-setback row
values.if_missing: The fetcher withholds flagged rows (#707) — verified live: 32 rows in DB, 31 served; the defective-source value can never render to a user until the user rules on it
Without the slug the gate returns None and every consumer skips DCP setbacks entirely for Wingecarribee addresses — the pre-change behaviour, fail-closed

values.value: dcp_version = 'Wingecarribee DCP 2010 town plans, as amended 2015'
values.read_at: row provenance for the DCP-2026 supersession swap
values.if_missing: Every row carries it; when the consolidated DCP 2026 commences, rows are identifiable and is_current versioning retires them cleanly

queries.purpose: Idempotent production load of 32 numeric controls plus lga_registry registration, dry-run first; verified post-load 32 rows present, 31 served (one withheld by needs_review)
queries.where_clause: duplicate check WHERE lga AND dev_type AND control_type AND COALESCE(condition); lga_registry ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING; inserts only, no DELETE or UPDATE

break_it.scenario: A value differs between the three town plans and the single-slug design serves Bowral's number to a Mittagong address
break_it.what_happens: Wrong council control rendered with a confident source citation — worse than absence
break_it.how: the Phase-0 probe compared the setback tables verbatim across all three town plans before the design was chosen (identical, including the same source typo); scope is limited to the shared Part C template and the dcp_version field names the town-plan basis

break_it.scenario: The defective source clause (missing height threshold) gets served with an interpreted value
break_it.what_happens: A number the council never published, rendered as if quoted — fabricated regulatory data
break_it.how: the row stores the verbatim defective text with [sic], needs_review=TRUE and a review_reason naming all three documents' page numbers; live verification shows the fetcher withholds it (31 of 32 served)
break_it.repro: SELECT needs_review, review_reason FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE lga='wingecarribee' AND needs_review

break_it.scenario: Re-running the insert script double-loads the rows
break_it.what_happens: Duplicate controls inflate or contradict the rendered values
break_it.how: per-row duplicate check on lga+dev_type+control_type+condition skips existing rows; the registry upsert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
break_it.repro: run the script twice; second run prints 32 SKIP (dup) and inserts nothing

break_it.scenario: The DCP 2026 consolidation commences and these town-plan rows silently keep serving stale controls
break_it.what_happens: Superseded numbers served with live-looking provenance
break_it.how: every row carries dcp_version naming the 2015-amended town plans and pdf_page into the archived reference PDF; is_current versioning is the established supersession mechanism; the onboarding plan file records the watch on the consolidation's adoption

break_it.scenario: A Wingecarribee village or rural lot (outside the three towns) gets town-plan numbers
break_it.what_happens: Controls from the wrong document family applied to Robertson/Berrima/rural addresses
break_it.how: accepted residual, conservative direction unavailable without per-document scoping: the three TOWN plans cover the population centres; village DCPs were not verified and their lots will currently receive the town-plan template values. Flagged for follow-up in the onboarding plan; the SEPP/LEP layers (which dominate eligibility) are per-lot regardless
break_it.repro: onboarding plan remaining-unknowns; village-plan comparison is the named follow-up
